title: The primary and secondary immune responses
caption: On first exposure to an antigen the antibody level takes one to two weeks to rise, and stays low. On re-exposure the memory cells respond within days: the antibody level rises faster, much higher and lasts longer. This is the principle behind vaccines and booster doses. Relative levels, drawn schematically.
alt: A curve of antibody level against days: a slow, low rise to a peak around day 14 after the first exposure, then after a second exposure at day 35 a much faster, taller peak around day 40.
description: First exposure (day 0): a lag, then antibody levels rise slowly to a low peak at about two weeks.
Second exposure (day 35): memory cells respond at once.
The secondary response peaks within days, about six times higher, and lasts longer.
A vaccine gives the first exposure safely, so the real infection meets a secondary response.
